opening: Will a bank lend against your assets, or against your cash flow?
linkedin:
Will a bank lend against your assets, or against your cash flow?

In our view, there are two broad approaches. Asset-backed lending leans on what you own: stock, receivables or property. Cash-flow lending leans on the cash the business generates to repay. Each bank sets its own criteria, so check your facility letter.

If a bank looks at cash flow, expect three questions: how much cash is left after costs, whether it is steady month to month, and whether it covers each repayment.

Which story will your numbers tell?
